title: Phase-Aware Spectral Entropy as a Diagnostic of Stream-Cipher IV Diffusion — Data and Code

creators.name: Augustynowicz, Paweł
creators.affiliation: Faculty of Cybernetics, Military University of Technology, Warsaw, Poland

description: Raw arrays, per-key and summary results, fixed protocols, code, vector checks, and the twelve-page Entropy manuscript on phase-aware spectral entropy as a diagnostic of stream-cipher IV response. A common 4096-bit output protocol covers Grain-128, Trivium, MICKEY 2.0, HC-128, Rabbit, ChaCha20, and Salsa20 in separately fixed cohorts (indices 280–439). A matched-nonce phase intervention uses fresh keys 440–519 and paired rotations; a descriptive benchmark compares direct and spectral statistics on those exact streams. A separately locked all-64-mask ARX study on indices 520–599 confirms the two-round Salsa20 nonce-word contrast and resolves compensating output-word responses in ChaCha20. Fresh-key Grain and Trivium probes on indices 600–679 validate an early IV-region gradient and investigate a short-initialization higher-order subcube front. An auxiliary A5/1 frame study uses standard 114-bit frame output, all 22 frame masks, and keys 680–759; an independent validation uses keys 760–839. It confirms a zero-clock loading gradient but detects no standard 100-clock signal in a corrected 44-cell search. The A5/1 test does not reproduce known state-recovery attacks. Graph-matched SHAKE256 controls and whole-key uncertainty calculations accompany each experiment. No result estimates keystream Shannon entropy or attack advantage.
